questions.prompt: How is Nova v2 configured and run safely? Explain what happens at boot when configuration is missing and where environment access is allowed, how the Docker image keeps credentials out and why passing secrets with -e is discouraged (and what to use instead), the container's user and health check design, and which Bedrock prerequisites to check before suspecting the code.

keyPoints.text: The server refuses to boot when a required environment variable (AWS_APP_ID, AWS_APP_SECRET, REGION) is missing and names every absent one.
keyPoints.quote:
The server refuses to boot with a missing
environment variable and names every one that is absent.

keyPoints.text: config.js is the designated home of environment access: it reads and validates process.env and returns a frozen config object that the rest of the app is handed (server.js only bridges the AWS credential names back into the environment).
keyPoints.quote: the only file that reads process.env

keyPoints.text: The image reads all configuration from the environment and never contains a .env file, because .dockerignore excludes it, so a credential cannot be baked in.
keyPoints.quote:
so a credential cannot be baked in by
accident.

keyPoints.text: Secrets passed with -e land in shell history and docker inspect; use --env-file from outside the build context or a platform secret store.
keyPoints.quote:
Passing secrets with `-e` puts them in your shell history and in
`docker inspect`.

keyPoints.text: The container runs as the unprivileged node user.
keyPoints.quote: The container runs as the unprivileged `node` user

keyPoints.text: Its HEALTHCHECK hits /health, which makes no AWS calls, so a Bedrock outage cannot mark a healthy container unhealthy.
keyPoints.quote:
so a Bedrock outage cannot mark an
otherwise healthy container unhealthy.

keyPoints.text: Claude model access must be enabled in the Bedrock console for the region, and current models generally need a cross-region inference profile.
keyPoints.quote:
current-generation models generally require a cross-region
inference profile

keyPoints.text: On AccessDeniedException or ValidationException, check that console setting before suspecting the code.
keyPoints.quote: check that console setting before suspecting the code.

questions.prompt: Where does Nova v2 draw its trust boundaries? Explain how it treats Claude's output when rendering it into the page, which links survive, where the one unescaped innerHTML is and why it is tolerated, what protection the API has in place of user authentication and what that means for deployment, and what the API tests guarantee about a 500 response.

keyPoints.text: Model output is treated as untrusted input to the DOM.
keyPoints.quote: Model output is untrusted input to the DOM.

keyPoints.text: public/js/markdown.js escapes everything before building markup.
keyPoints.quote:
escapes
everything before building markup

keyPoints.text: Only http(s) links are turned into anchors.
keyPoints.quote:
only `http(s)` links are turned into
anchors.

keyPoints.text: The one innerHTML that builds markup from values without escaping them is in nav.js; it is tolerated only because those values are a hardcoded constant, and it should stay that way.
keyPoints.quote:
The single unescaped `innerHTML` in the codebase is in `nav.js`, over a
hardcoded constant.

keyPoints.text: There is no user authentication.
keyPoints.quote: There is no user authentication.

keyPoints.text: CORS is restricted to ALLOWED_ORIGINS and the costly endpoints (/speak, /ask-claude, /get-signed-url) are rate limited, but that is a speed bump, not auth.
keyPoints.quote: that is a speed bump, not auth.

keyPoints.text: So the app must not be exposed to the public internet as it stands.
keyPoints.quote:
Do not
expose this to the public internet as it stands.

keyPoints.text: The API tests check that a 500 leaks neither the AWS error nor a stack trace.
keyPoints.quote:
a 500 leaks neither the AWS error
  nor a stack trace.

questions.prompt: Trace Nova v2's audio and streaming design: where the PCM conversion runs and what the main thread is left doing, how the sample rate reaches Transcribe and who resamples, how /ask-claude streams to the browser and the one framing rule SSE must obey (and how that rule is guarded), and what the audio-utils tests pin down.

keyPoints.text: Audio conversion runs on the audio thread: pcm-worklet.js converts Float32 to Int16 inside the worklet.
keyPoints.quote: Audio conversion happens on the audio thread.

keyPoints.text: The worklet transfers buffers to the main thread, which only frames and sends them.
keyPoints.quote:
transfers buffers to the main
thread, which only frames and sends.

keyPoints.text: The sample rate is negotiated, not resampled in the page.
keyPoints.quote: Sample rate is negotiated, not resampled.

keyPoints.text: The page asks for a 16 kHz AudioContext, reads back what it actually got, and reports that via ?sampleRate=.
keyPoints.quote: reads back what it actually got, and tells Transcribe the truth

keyPoints.text: AWS does any resampling that is needed.
keyPoints.quote: AWS resamples if needed.

keyPoints.text: /ask-claude streams as SSE (with ?stream=1) and the chat page reads it with a fetch stream reader.
keyPoints.quote: `routes/claude.js` (SSE), `public/js/chat.js` (fetch stream reader)

keyPoints.text: Every SSE frame must end with a blank line or the browser buffers the response forever; a test guards this.
keyPoints.quote:
or the browser buffers the
response forever.

keyPoints.text: audio-utils tests check CRC-32 against the published check vector and PCM conversion including clamping and the asymmetric ±1 scale.
keyPoints.quote:
PCM
  conversion including clamping and the asymmetric ±1 scale
